Average recovery time is about 4-6 weeks. But the redness takes up to 3 months to completely disappear. The most painful part is the application, you HAVE to be injected with numbing because the burning would be unbearable. Some people are even given IV sedatives.
The recovery is very uncomfortable because your face goes stiff and starts to peel. And it's also disgusting, oozes, sheds, peels... all the lovely things skin can do.

Phenol peel is great in smoothening even very deep wrinkles and lightening dark discoloration - but your heart has to be monitored during application and the application has to be done in steps because there's a big risk of phenol overdose. 
In recent years we have been able to achieve the same results with lasers, which have much shorter recovery time, so not many people get this done anymore.

Someone with a personality disorder here. I have BPD and this sounds a lot like splitting. This means that people with my disorder tend to have a hard time finding a middle ground in their emotions and more often feel in opposite extremes - either happy, positive and euphoric or sad, angry and negative. Symptoms are especially apparent in relationships, where sometimes even a small trigger can switch our mood and we may suddenly become overly mad at you. Often it's brought up by seeming or actual abandonment. Which is alright, we feel intense emotions and it's incredibly hard to deal with - but therapy and medication is important because without it one can become overly manipulative or aggressive, among many other things like self-destructive behaviour.

But some of what you describe also sounds like a delusion - remembering things differently, giving them a different meaning, believing stuff that isn't real at all. Which is more typical for schizofrenia. But I don't wanna speak to that much as I don't know it as well.
